title: Meta Muse Code pricing: what a free coding agent really costs | eesel AI

facts.fact: Per eesel's reading of Meta's pricing, Muse Code itself is free and Meta charges for the underlying model, at $1.25 per million input tokens, $0.15 cached, and $4.25 output on muse-spark-1.2.
facts.quote: Muse Code costs nothing. Meta charges you for the model underneath it: $1.25 per million input tokens, $0.15 cached, and $4.25 output on `muse-spark-1.2`

facts.fact: The contributor tier for muse-spark-1.2 is priced at $0.10 input, $0.002 cached, and $0.20 output per million tokens, for users who let Meta train on their code.
facts.quote: $0.10 / $0.002 / $0.20 on the contributor tier if you let Meta train on your code

facts.fact: eesel states that Meta's pricing, product, and billing pages list no seat price, subscription, free tier, or trial credit for Muse Code.
facts.quote: There is no seat price, no subscription, no free tier, and no trial credit anywhere on Meta's pricing, product, or billing pages.

facts.fact: Muse Code was shipped in beta on 5 August 2026 alongside the Muse Spark 1.2 model.
facts.quote: shipped in beta on 5 August 2026 alongside the Muse Spark 1.2 model

facts.fact: Web search grounding is the only add-on meter, charged at $2.50 per 1,000 queries on top of tokens.
facts.quote: There is one genuine add-on meter, web search grounding at **$2.50 per 1,000 queries**

facts.fact: muse-spark-1.1 is priced the same as muse-spark-1.2, at $1.25 input, $0.15 cached, and $4.25 output per million tokens.
Rate limits apply per team rather than per key.
facts.quote: Rate limits apply per team rather than per key, so extra keys buy you nothing.

facts.fact: Background submissions carry a separate cap of 600 requests per minute.
facts.quote: Background submissions carry a third cap of 600 per minute on top.

facts.fact: Meta's configuration docs state that the default model is muse-spark-1.2.
Meta's launch blog says Muse Code starts on a contributor tier, which conflicts with the configuration docs on the default model.
Meta states there is no long-context premium, so the same rate applies regardless of how full the context window is.
facts.quote: There is no long-context premium: you pay the same rate whether your context window is mostly empty or almost full.

facts.fact: Meta says the system prompt and scaffolding tokens it injects into every prompt are not billed.
facts.quote: those injected tokens are not billed.

facts.fact: Muse Code has no cache-write fee, and caching is automatic.
Background responses via background: true are not discounted, and there is no batch discount.
facts.quote: `background: true` responses exist but are not discounted.

facts.fact: Meta's pricing page states there are no minimums or upfront commitment.
eesel claims Muse Code ships with its reasoning effort at the second-highest of seven settings by default.
facts.quote: at the second-highest reasoning setting of seven

facts.fact: eesel says Meta ships no spend cap of any kind for Muse Code, and the only limit in the billing docs is a payment threshold.
facts.quote: Meta ships no spend cap of any kind.

facts.fact: eesel's own support product charges 1 credit per ticket or chat on a fixed monthly price starting at $299/month for 500 credits.
The muse-spark-1.2 context window is 1,048,576 tokens.
The article was last edited on August 17, 2026.
